patients.summary: Elementary school teacher with generalized anxiety on sertraline who joins in 2021. Her 2023 delivery is followed by peripartum cardiomyopathy (LVEF 35%, recovered to 55%) and postpartum thyroiditis; a twin pregnancy ends in an emergency cesarean for vasa previa in 2025, then impaired glucose tolerance after diet-controlled gestational diabetes, and a fourth pregnancy ends in a planned repeat cesarean in 2026.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
30F here to establish. Teaches second grade in the district, married, no kids yet.

HPI: Generalized anxiety since about 2016 — worry that "runs in the background," worse in August before the school year and around evaluations. Has been on sertraline 50 mg daily since, which she feels is the right dose. No panic attacks lately. Sleeping ok most nights. Denies low mood, no SI.

PMH: GAD. Gallstones found on an US in 2018 after one episode of upper abdominal pain that settled on its own; never had surgery, no attacks since.
PSH: D&C 2019 (early pregnancy loss).
OB: G1P0, one early loss.
Meds: sertraline 50 mg daily.
Allergies: sulfa, latex (she doesn't remember the reactions).
FH: mother type 2 diabetes. Maternal aunt with an autoimmune thyroid problem. Paternal grandmother had dilated cardiomyopathy.
SH: never smoker, no alcohol, no drugs. Walks most evenings.

ROS: negative in detail except as above.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well appearing, pleasant. HEENT normal. Neck supple, thyroid normal size, no nodules. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no RUQ tenderness. Ext no edema. Skin no rashes. Neuro nonfocal. Mood good, affect bright.

GAD-7 6, PHQ-9 3.

A/P
1. GAD — stable on sertraline 50, continue. Refills sent. Reassess at each visit.
2. Cholelithiasis, asymptomatic — no action; reviewed what biliary colic feels like.
3. Health maintenance — Pap/HPV 2020 negative, next 2025. COVID primary series done. Flu shot when available in Oct. Screening labs today incl HIV and hep C once.
4. Allergies sulfa/latex entered.

RTC 1 yr for physical, sooner prn. She can text with questions.

Allergies: sulfa, latex.
FH: mother T2DM, maternal aunt autoimmune thyroid disease, paternal GM dilated cardiomyopathy. No changes.
SH: teacher, never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight 59 kg. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender. No edema. Normal affect.

A/P:
- GAD — stable, continue sertraline.
- Preconception — start an OTC prenatal vitamin daily, added to med list. If not pregnant after a year of trying, let us know and we can start a workup or send to GYN.

documents.author: PCP

Your anxiety has been well controlled on it and stopping suddenly is the bigger risk. Your OB will go over it too. Keep up the prenatal vitamin. Due date by your LMP is around 10/2. Message me any time.

documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside OB/GYN office note, visit 10/30/2023.

Reason: still bleeding at four weeks after vaginal delivery.

Ms. Dion is 4 weeks out from a term vaginal birth (10/2/23). She has had bleeding every day since delivery — heavy and bright red at first, and now light and brown. She has had no fevers, no pelvic or abdominal pain, and no malodorous discharge. Exclusively breastfeeding, going well.

History: GAD on sertraline 50 mg daily. Prior D&C (2019). Prenatal vitamin daily.
Allergies: sulfa drugs, latex.

Exam: vital signs stable, afebrile. Abdomen soft and non-tender, fundus not palpable. Perineum: episiotomy repair well healed. No lacerations or other trauma of the lower genital tract. Small amount of brown lochia.

Labs: CBC today normal.

Assessment: lochia that is tapering normally at 4 weeks; normal blood count.
Plan: reassurance. Return or call for heavy bleeding, fever or pain. Continue breastfeeding. Routine postpartum visit at 6-8 weeks.

orders.reason: Postpartum dyspnea, orthopnea and edema; evaluate for peripartum cardiomyopathy

documents.title: Office Visit — Dyspnea and Edema
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Texted Sunday night that she can't catch her breath on the stairs; seen same day today. 7 weeks postpartum (SVD 10/2), breastfeeding.

S: Says she has been short of breath since the last few weeks of the pregnancy, figured it was the baby pushing up, but instead of getting better after delivery it has gotten worse. Now gets winded going up one flight with the baby. Has to prop on two pillows at night, lying flat feels uncomfortable. Ankles puffy by evening. Very tired, though she has a 7-week-old. No chest pain, no palpitations, no fever or cough, no calf pain. No travel.

FH: paternal grandmother had dilated cardiomyopathy.
Meds: sertraline 50, prenatal vitamin.
Allergies: sulfa, latex.

O: Vitals as charted. Weight 64 kg, up from her pre-pregnancy ~59. Tired appearing, speaking full sentences. JVP hard to assess with her positioning. Heart regular, no murmur heard. Lungs: fine crackles at both bases. Abdomen soft. 2+ pitting edema both ankles, calves soft and nontender.

GAD-7 7 — mostly worry about this.

A/P:
Postpartum dyspnea with orthopnea, edema and basilar crackles — I'm worried about peripartum cardiomyopathy until proven otherwise, especially with the family history of DCM.
- Called cardiology directly; they can see her Friday 11/24. Referral placed.
- CBC and BMP today.
- Strict ED precautions reviewed with her and husband on speaker: chest pain, breathlessness at rest, can't lie down at all, fainting — go to the ED, don't wait for Friday.
- OK to keep breastfeeding.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lily — blood count normal (no anemia), and kidney function, potassium and sodium are normal. Still want you to keep the cardiology appointment Friday. How are you feeling this morning?

documents.title: RE: Lab Results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: About the same, thanks for checking. Will be there Friday.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every morning

documents.title: Cardiology Consultation (received)
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group — new consultation 11/24/2023

Dear Doctor,
Thank you for the same-week referral of Ms. Lily Dion, 32, seen today about seven and a half weeks after a term vaginal delivery on 10/2/23. She had a visit with her obstetrician a few weeks ago for prolonged lochia, which settled.

HPI: Her breathing began to bother her late in the third trimester and has steadily worsened rather than improved since the birth. She now has to stop partway up a single flight of stairs, finds lying flat uncomfortable, and notices ankle swelling by the end of each day. She is more fatigued than she expects to be and has had some difficulty sleeping. She denies chest pain, palpitations, fever and recent travel.

PMH: generalized anxiety disorder. Prior D&C. G2P1011.
Medications: sertraline 50 mg daily; prenatal vitamin.
Allergies: sulfa drugs, latex.
Family history: paternal grandmother with dilated cardiomyopathy; mother with type 2 diabetes; maternal aunt with autoimmune thyroid disease.
Social: elementary school teacher; never smoker; no alcohol.

Exam: BP 112/76, HR 92, RR 18, BMI 25. Appears tired but comfortable at rest. JVP mildly elevated. Fine crackles at both lung bases; lungs resonant to percussion without wheeze. Regular rhythm, no murmur or gallop. Bilateral 2+ pitting edema of the lower legs.

Data: urine hCG negative today.

Impression: new heart failure symptoms beginning in late pregnancy and persisting postpartum, with volume overload on exam. Peripartum cardiomyopathy is the leading concern given the timing and family history.

Plan:
1. Transthoracic echocardiogram — scheduled 11/28.
2. Furosemide 20 mg each morning for congestion; daily weights.
3. Further therapy per echo; she is breastfeeding and we will choose agents compatible with nursing.
4. ED for rest dyspnea or chest pain.

Sincerely,
Cardiology

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily
Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with food

reports.text: Indication: postpartum dyspnea and edema. Technically adequate study. Left ventricle normal in size with globally reduced systolic function; global hypokinesis without regional predominance. LVEF 35% by biplane Simpson. Right ventricle normal size and function. Atria normal size. Mitral, aortic, tricuspid and pulmonic valves structurally normal without significant stenosis or regurgitation. No pericardial effusion. IVC normal caliber.
reports.conclusion: Reduced LV systolic function, LVEF 35%, global hypokinesis. No valvular abnormality.

documents.title: Cardiology Echo Result and Plan (received)
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Cardiology telephone follow-up 11/28/2023 — copy to PCP.

Echo today: LVEF 35% with global hypokinesis, valves normal. In the setting of heart failure that began in late pregnancy and the early postpartum period with no other cause identified, this is peripartum cardiomyopathy.

Discussed with patient by phone. Starting:
- enalapril 5 mg twice daily
- carvedilol 3.125 mg twice daily
Both are acceptable while breastfeeding. Continue furosemide 20 mg daily. BMP in about 1 week — her PCP's lab will draw it. Follow-up visit early January to titrate. Repeat echo after 3 months of therapy.

Counseled on low-salt diet, daily weights, and symptoms that need the ED.

documents.title: Heart Medicines and Nursing
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi. Cardiology called with the echo, I have peripartum cardiomyopathy. I'm honestly freaking out a little. They started two new pills plus the water pill. They said they're ok with breastfeeding but I wanted to hear it from you too. Also is it ok with the sertraline?

documents.title: RE: Heart Medicines and Nursing
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lily, I saw the report and I'm glad you're with that team. Enalapril and carvedilol are both used in nursing mothers and are fine with sertraline. Many women with this condition get a lot of their heart function back over the next several months on these medicines. Please take them as prescribed, weigh yourself every morning, and text me if your weight jumps or breathing gets worse. Want a quick visit next week to talk it through? No charge for that, it's what we're here for.

documents.title: RE: Heart Medicines and Nursing
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you. That helps. I'll text if anything changes. I think I'm ok for now.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your kidney function and potassium are normal on the new enalapril. I sent a copy to cardiology.

documents.title: Leave Extension Form
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Pt called — district needs a provider form to extend her leave past winter break because of the heart diagnosis. Form uploaded. PCP to complete; cardiology note supports. Pt aware it takes 3-5 business days.

PCP: completed, return to work date to be reassessed after her January cardiology visit. Faxed to HR, copy to pt.

Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with food

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up (received)
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Cardiology follow-up, 1/8/2024.

Peripartum cardiomyopathy, LVEF 35% on 11/28. Since starting therapy she is breathing better, sleeping flat, swelling gone. Weight down about 1.5 kg. Tolerating medicines without dizziness. Still breastfeeding.

Exam: vitals as recorded. JVP normal. Lungs clear. Regular, no gallop. No edema.
BMP 12/6 (PCP lab) reviewed — normal.

Assessment: PPCM, euvolemic on current therapy.
Plan:
- Stop furosemide.
- Enalapril to 10 mg twice daily.
- Carvedilol to 6.25 mg twice daily.
- Repeat echo in the spring.
- Return 4-6 weeks; sooner for weight gain over 2 lb in a day or 5 lb in a week, or breathlessness.
Allergies: sulfa, latex.

events.reason: Shortness of breath, orthopnea, leg swelling

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every morning

reports.text: PA and lateral views. The cardiac silhouette is enlarged. Pulmonary vascular congestion with indistinct vascular markings. No focal consolidation. No pneumothorax. Osseous structures unremarkable.
Sinus tachycardia. Normal axis. Normal intervals. No ST-segment elevation or depression. No pathologic Q waves.
reports.conclusion: Sinus tachycardia without ST changes or Q waves.

reports.text: Limited study from the emergency department. Left ventricular systolic function globally reduced with diffuse hypokinesis; LVEF estimated 35%. Right ventricular function preserved. Valves without structural abnormality, stenosis or significant regurgitation. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: LVEF 35% with global hypokinesis; no valvular abnormality.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record (received)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department — physician record, 1/29/2024.

CC: worsening breathlessness and leg swelling.

HPI: 32F, about 4 months after a vaginal delivery (her first child), with peripartum cardiomyopathy diagnosed by her cardiologist two months ago and followed there. Over the last 2 weeks she has become progressively more short of breath, now needs to sleep propped up, and both legs have swollen again. Her furosemide was stopped at a cardiology visit about three weeks ago. No chest pain.

Meds: enalapril 10 mg BID, carvedilol 6.25 mg BID, sertraline 50 mg daily. Took prenatal vitamins through the pregnancy.
Allergies: sulfa, latex.
Social: no tobacco, alcohol or drugs.

Exam: BP 110/70, HR 102, RR 22, SpO2 94% RA. Mildly dyspneic. Rales at both bases. S3 present. Pitting edema 2+ bilaterally to mid-shin.

Results: Hgb 12.5, WBC 7.5, plt 250. Na 138, K 4.2, Cr 0.9. BNP 900. Troponin I <0.04.
CXR: cardiomegaly, pulmonary vascular congestion.
ECG: sinus tachycardia, no ST changes, no Q waves.
Echo (bedside formal, cardiology read): EF 35%, global hypokinesis, valves normal.

ED course: furosemide 40 mg IV with brisk diuresis. Breathing improved, sitting comfortably, SpO2 97% on room air by midnight. Discussed with on-call cardiology: acceptable for discharge with close follow-up given rapid response.

Impression: acute on chronic systolic heart failure, peripartum cardiomyopathy.
Disposition: home. Restart furosemide 20 mg by mouth every morning. Continue enalapril and carvedilol. Cardiology within 1-2 weeks; PCP within a few days. Return for worse breathing, chest pain, fainting.

documents.title: Post-ED Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called after ED notification. Got home after midnight, peeing a lot this morning after furosemide, breathing much easier, slept on 2 pillows. Home scale weight down from yesterday. Has all meds, took furosemide 20 at 7 am. Feeding baby ok. Booked with PCP Thu 2/1. Cardiology appt 2/12 confirmed by pt. Reviewed red flags.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit — Post-ED
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after ED visit Monday for HF exacerbation (PPCM, EF 35%). Treated with IV furosemide and sent home on furosemide 20 daily.

S: Much better. Sleeping on one pillow again, swelling nearly gone, can do the stairs with the baby slowly. Home weights trending down. Taking everything: enalapril 10 bid, carvedilol 6.25 bid, furosemide 20 qAM, sertraline 50, prenatal vitamin. Mild lightheadedness standing up fast, no falls. Still nursing. Anxious — "every time I get winded I think it's happening again." GAD-7 8.

O: Vitals as charted. Lungs clear today. Regular rhythm, no gallop heard. Trace ankle edema only. Weight 63 kg.

A/P:
1. PPCM with recent decompensation, now improved on diuretic. Continue regimen. BMP today on ACE-I + loop. Cardiology 2/12. Daily weights, call for gain of 3 lb overnight or 5 lb in a week.
2. GAD — understandably up. Continue sertraline 50; we talked through a plan for the scary moments (check weight, sit up, text us). She declines a dose change for now.
3. Return to work — not yet; revisit after cardiology. Updated leave form.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your potassium and kidney function are normal on the furosemide and enalapril. Keep going as you are.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up (received)
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Cardiology follow-up 2/12/2024 after ED visit for decompensation.

Feels well. No orthopnea. Walking 20 minutes without stopping. Weight stable at home. Euvolemic on exam: JVP flat, lungs clear, no S3 today, no edema. BMP from 2/1 normal.

PPCM, improving clinically.
- Continue enalapril 10 mg BID, carvedilol 6.25 mg BID, furosemide 20 mg daily for now.
- Echo in about 3 months (May).
- Cleared to return to teaching in March if she stays well; letter given.
Allergies: sulfa, latex.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Visit — Palpitations
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, she asked for today after texting this morning.

S: Back at school 2 weeks. Over the past few weeks her heart has been racing at rest, she feels jittery and snappy with the kids and her husband, and she has lost about 10 lb since November despite eating more than usual. She worried it was her heart again, but no orthopnea, no swelling, weights on her scale have gone down, not up. No neck pain or tenderness. Still breastfeeding, about 5 1/2 months postpartum. No new meds or supplements.
FH: maternal aunt with autoimmune thyroid disease.

O: Video — appears a little restless, speech fast but organized. No visible neck swelling. Her watch has been showing a fast resting heart rate.

A/P:
Postpartum palpitations, irritability, weight loss with increased appetite — postpartum thyroid dysfunction is high on the list; also want to make sure the cardiomyopathy is not the driver.
- TSH, free T4, total T3 tomorrow morning at our lab.
- Continue carvedilol (which will blunt some of this).
- If chest pain, fainting or breathing worse, ED.

documents.title: Thyroid Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt before school with results: TSH suppressed (<0.01), free T4 2.5 and total T3 200, both high. So her thyroid is overactive, which fits her symptoms. Most likely postpartum thyroiditis (temporary inflammation of the thyroid after pregnancy), though Graves disease has to be excluded since the treatment is different. Expedited endocrinology referral placed — I called their office, they will fit her in next week. Keep carvedilol. She asked about nursing — fine for now; endocrinology may want an uptake scan, which would mean a short pause, they will go over it.

documents.title: Endocrinology Consultation (received)
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology — new patient consultation, 3/22/2024

Referred by her PCP for thyrotoxicosis about five and a half months after delivery.

HPI: 33-year-old woman, delivered 10/2/23, with peripartum cardiomyopathy diagnosed in November and treated by cardiology (seen in the ED in January). She describes several weeks of a racing heart, short temper, and a weight loss of around ten pounds even though she is hungrier than usual. No pain, tenderness or fullness in the neck. No eye symptoms.

Medications: enalapril 10 mg BID, carvedilol 6.25 mg BID, furosemide 20 mg daily, sertraline 50 mg daily, prenatal vitamin.
Allergies: sulfa drugs, latex.
Family history: maternal aunt with autoimmune thyroid disease; mother with type 2 diabetes; paternal grandmother with dilated cardiomyopathy.
Social: teacher, never smoker, no alcohol. Breastfeeding.

Exam: HR 102. Fine tremor of the hands with arms extended. Thyroid not enlarged, no nodules felt, non-tender. Skin warm and slightly moist. No proptosis or lid lag.

Labs (3/13, PCP): TSH <0.01, free T4 2.5 ng/dL, total T3 200 ng/dL.

Assessment: postpartum thyrotoxicosis. Painless postpartum thyroiditis is most likely; Graves disease needs to be excluded.
Plan:
- Radioactive iodine uptake 3/25. We discussed breastfeeding: she will pump ahead, stop nursing for the period nuclear medicine advises, and discard milk expressed during that window.
- No antithyroid drug pending the uptake; she is already on carvedilol, which helps the adrenergic symptoms.
- Will call with the result.

reports.text: Radioiodine (I-123) uptake measured at 4 and 24 hours with imaging of the thyroid bed. Uptake is low at both time points, well below the normal range, with faint, homogeneous thyroid visualization. No focal hot or cold areas.
reports.conclusion: Low radioiodine uptake, consistent with thyroiditis rather than Graves disease.

documents.title: Endocrinology Addendum (received)
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Addendum to 3/22 consult. Uptake scan 3/25: low uptake. This confirms postpartum thyroiditis in its hyperthyroid phase; Graves disease is not supported.

Plan: no antithyroid medication (it does not help thyroiditis). Continue carvedilol per cardiology for rate and symptoms. Repeat TSH and free T4 in about 6 weeks — PCP is happy to draw. A hypothyroid phase can follow over the next few months; if TSH rises we will consider levothyroxine. She may resume breastfeeding after the advised interval. Patient informed by phone.

documents.title: Feeling Better
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just an update — the racing heart is a lot better the last week or so and I'm not as short with everyone lol. Back to nursing after the scan, no problems. When do you want the thyroid labs? Also I need a refill on the carvedilol, pharmacy said no refills left.

documents.title: RE: Feeling Better
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great news. Labs the first week of May — I put in TSH and free T4 plus a BMP; any morning at our lab. Carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily sent with refills (cardiology is fine with us refilling).

reports.text: Comparison 11/28/2023. Left ventricle normal in size with normal wall motion throughout. LVEF 55% by biplane method. Normal diastolic filling for age. Right ventricle normal. Valves structurally normal without significant regurgitation. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Normal LV size and systolic function, LVEF 55% (previously 35%). No valvular abnormality.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up (received)
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Cardiology follow-up 5/13/2024 with echo.

She feels back to normal and is teaching full days. Thyroid symptoms settling.
Echo today: LVEF 55%, normal wall motion — recovery of LV function from 35% in November.

Assessment: peripartum cardiomyopathy with recovered ejection fraction.
Plan:
- Stop furosemide.
- Continue enalapril 10 mg BID and carvedilol 6.25 mg BID; we will not withdraw therapy within the first year of recovery.
- Discussed that any future pregnancy carries a risk that the cardiomyopathy recurs, and should be planned together with us and her obstetrician. Enalapril must be stopped as soon as she is pregnant.
- Return 6 months, echo in a year.
Allergies: sulfa, latex.

documents.title: Office Visit — Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up thyroid and PPCM.

S: Feels like herself. No palpitations, appetite normal, weight back up a little. Weaned the baby over the last few weeks (7 1/2 months), on formula and starting solids. Echo last week EF 55% — cardiology stopped furosemide, continuing enalapril/carvedilol. No orthopnea, no edema. Anxiety "way better now that everything's calmer." Teaching full days.

Labs 5/6: TSH 1.9, free T4 1.1 — normal. BMP normal.

O: Vitals as charted, weight 60 kg. No tremor. Thyroid normal size, nontender. Heart regular, no gallop. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P:
1. Postpartum thyroiditis, hyperthyroid phase — resolved, euthyroid now. She remains at risk for a later hypothyroid phase and for recurrence after future pregnancies; recheck TSH if fatigue, weight gain or cold intolerance, and with any future postpartum period.
2. PPCM, recovered EF on enalapril and carvedilol — per cardiology. Reinforced their advice: if she becomes pregnant, stop enalapril right away and call both offices.
3. GAD — stable on sertraline.
4. Breastfeeding completed.
Physical due August.

- Continue sertraline 50 and prenatal vitamin.
- I messaged her cardiologist this morning; they will see her with an echo in the next few weeks and coordinate with high-risk OB.
- She will call her OB today for an early appointment.
She is anxious but has a plan. Text with any breathlessness, swelling or palpitations.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record (received)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department, 2/6/2025, with obstetrics at bedside.

CC: vaginal bleeding, 37 weeks with twins.

HPI: 33-year-old G3P1011 at 37w3d with dichorionic diamniotic twins. About an hour before arrival she felt a sudden "pop" low in her abdomen and then began bleeding vaginally. The bleeding is not painful, has not stopped, and appears to be increasing. No fall, blow or other trauma. She feels the babies moving. Background: peripartum cardiomyopathy after her 2023 delivery with recovered function; postpartum thyroiditis in 2024. Her first child was born vaginally at term without difficulty. This pregnancy has gone smoothly apart from gestational diabetes controlled with diet, and her ultrasounds have been normal.

Meds: carvedilol 6.25 mg BID, sertraline 50 mg daily, prenatal vitamin.
Allergies: sulfa drugs, latex.

Exam: vital signs stable. Continuous fetal monitoring: both tracings reassuring. Sterile speculum: blood coming through the cervical os; vaginal walls and cervix themselves are not bleeding.

Labs: Hgb 12.2, platelets 250, PT 12 s, aPTT 30 s.

Bedside ultrasound by OB: fetal vessels running across the internal os.

Impression: vasa previa with bleeding after rupture of membranes, term twin gestation requiring delivery now.
Disposition: taken directly to the operating room by obstetrics for emergency cesarean delivery. Latex-free room. Anesthesia and cardiology notified.

Still thirsty and peeing more than she used to, though she is nursing twins and drinking a lot of water. No weight loss, no vision change. Breastfeeding most feeds.

   - A1c again in about 6 months, or yearly.
2. Thirst/urination — UA today; likely nursing-related, but checking.
3. Postpartum thyroiditis history — TSH today.
4. PPCM — stable per cardiology.

documents.title: Obstetrics Prenatal Visit (received)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside OB/GYN — prenatal visit 1/26/2026, copy to primary care.

34-year-old G4P2013 at 33w0d, singleton. Background: peripartum cardiomyopathy after her 2023 delivery, recovered; vasa previa with emergency cesarean for twins in 2/2025; generalized anxiety disorder; impaired glucose tolerance; postpartum thyroiditis in 2024.

She came today mainly to ask that this baby be delivered by planned cesarean. She describes a great deal of fear about going through labor and a vaginal birth this time — much more than with her first, which was an easy term vaginal delivery of a 3500 g baby. No bleeding, no fluid leaking, no contractions. This pregnancy has been unremarkable: glucose testing normal, blood pressures normal with no gestational hypertension.

Meds: carvedilol 6.25 mg BID, sertraline 50 mg daily, prenatal vitamin.
Allergies: sulfa drugs, latex.

Exam: BP 120/78, HR 82. Nonstress test reactive and reassuring, no decelerations.

Counseling: with one prior low transverse cesarean she is a candidate for either a trial of labor after cesarean or a planned repeat cesarean. We went through the benefits and risks of each for this pregnancy and for future ones. She has thought about it carefully and is firm in choosing a repeat cesarean; her anxiety is a legitimate part of that decision.

Plan: planned repeat cesarean at 39 weeks — booked 3/9/2026. Anesthesia and cardiology aware; latex-free. Weekly visits from 36 weeks. Encouraged her to talk with her PCP about anxiety support in the meantime.

Sleeping 5-6 h. No panic attacks. Mood otherwise ok, still enjoying the kids and her class. No SI. Taking sertraline 50 daily.
GAD-7 12.

O: On video, tearful at moments, organized, good insight.

A/P: GAD with a flare in late pregnancy, tied to the prior emergency delivery and fear of labor.
- Offered a sertraline increase to 100 mg; she prefers to stay at 50 mg for the last weeks and revisit after delivery. Reasonable.
- Talked through what the planned delivery will look like vs last time; she found that helpful.
- Check-in by text weekly; postpartum visit with me 2-3 weeks after delivery, with mood screening.
